In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chandra survey of the galactic disk has been a success.
the ChaMPlane survey has been successful in its primary goal of identifying the origin and evolution of neutron stars and black hole binaries.

the ChaMPlane Survey is a unique project that combines the Chandra X-ray Observatory and the NOAO Long term Survey program to conduct an unprecedented multi-wavelength survey of the galactic bulge and plane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a unique and powerful tool in the ChaMPlane survey to study the galactic plane in X-ray, optical, and infrared bands.
we have identified a number of new neutron stars, black holes and Be X-ray binaries, and that the ChaMPlane X-ray and optical surveys provide a unique opportunity to study the galactic plane.
the ChaMPlane Survey is a unique project in the sense that it is an X-ray survey of the galactic disk, and the first to use the Chandra data for such a survey.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ChaMPlane Survey is a unique, multiwavelength survey of the galactic disk that is complementary to other large scale surveys, and that the combination of X-ray, optical, and IR data will be useful for studying the evolution of X-ray binaries.
the X-ray sky is not uniform in the galactic plane, and that the X-ray and optical properties of the sources are correlated with their location in the galactic disk.

the Chandra ACIS-I and -S surveys are ideal tools to study the galactic plane, and the ChaMPlane survey is a powerful tool to constrain the galactic population and evolution of neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes.
